summary: An informational memo describing procedures for a graceful move from an ATMARP-based Logical IP Subnet to an NHRP-based network model over ATM.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo explains how NHRP servers can support ATMARP clients during a transition to NHRP. It sets rules for requests, cache entries, and when direct connections may be offered.

questions: how to migrate classical ip over atm to nhrp
how do nhrp servers support atmarp clients
what is the atmarp to nhrp transition
when can an nhrp server deny direct resolution
subtitle: Transition procedures for coexisting ATMARP and NHRP clients on ATM networks.

tldr.problem: ATM networks may have ATMARP clients and NHRP clients at the same time while moving to NHRP for address resolution.
tldr.mechanism: NHRP servers in a logical IP subnet respond to ATMARP client requests using ATMARP behavior and mark resulting cache entries as ATMARP-sourced.
tldr.outcome: The memo defines coexistence rules for the transition and restricts its scope to switched virtual circuit environments using ATM AAL5 and IP.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 2336 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo describes a transition procedure for IP over ATM.

sections.title: Why a Transition Is Needed
sections.content:
ATMARP applies classical IP and ARP to ATM networks configured as logical IP subnets. NHRP lets a host or router discover network-layer and ATM next-hop addresses for reaching a destination.

The RFC expects ATMARP and NHRP clients to coexist during migration. It therefore requires NHRP servers to answer ATMARP client queries in a way that allows existing ATMARP clients to continue working. It places no protocol requirements on ATMARP servers.
sections.plainLanguage: During migration, older ATMARP clients and newer NHRP clients may share a subnet. The new servers need to understand requests from the older clients.

sections.title: NHRP Server Requirements
sections.content:
A logical IP subnet using NHRP uses NHRP servers rather than a mixture of NHRP servers and ATMARP servers. For a subnet containing both client types, NHRP servers MUST recognize ATMARP packets and respond as an ATMARP server would.

When a valid ATMARP request creates or updates a cache entry, the entry is marked as type ATMARP. A request for an off-subnet protocol address must not receive a normal ATMARP reply; the server sends an ATMARP negative acknowledgment instead. The default cache holding time for an ATMARP-created entry is 20 minutes.
sections.plainLanguage: NHRP servers handle valid ATMARP requests during coexistence and label the resulting cache entries so they can be distinguished from NHRP entries.

sections.title: Limits on Direct Resolution
sections.content:
An NHRP server must not send a positive resolution reply to a requester outside the target station's logical IP subnet when that target registered through ATMARP. The RFC says such a station is almost certainly not prepared to accept a cut-through virtual circuit.

The server returns an administratively prohibited result. This prevents setting up a direct circuit but does not prevent the requester from sending data along the routed path. The procedures cover switched virtual circuits, not permanent virtual circuits.
sections.plainLanguage: The server does not promise a direct circuit to an ATMARP client for an outside-subnet requester. The requester can still use the routed path.
